title: Berlin human L2/3 slices show a 1.9-fold shallow-to-deep connection bias without reciprocity excess; proofread mouse EM axons show no depth bias, and unproofread EM axons give a false one
abstract: We tested two reported properties of human layer 2/3 excitatory wiring: no reciprocity excess and a preference for deeper targets. We used the same estimators in Berlin human slice tables (4,299 pairs, 23 donors), Allen human slices (472 pairs, 45 donors), Allen mouse slices (2,377 pairs) and the MICrONS mouse V1 EM connectome (19,707 layer 2/3 pyramidal cells). With connection counts fixed per recording and distance bin, reciprocity ratios were 0.96 (95% donor interval 0.72 to 1.18) in Berlin, 1.24 (0.93 to 1.57) in Allen human and 1.68 (1.26 to 2.13) in mouse slices. Thus most of the pooled Allen human excess (2.27) came from density differences, and the two human datasets did not differ clearly. When each Berlin cell kept its in-degree and out-degree, reciprocity was in excess (1.28, 1.10 to 1.46), because shallower cells act as sources. In Berlin, the shallower-to-deeper connection rate was 1.90 times the reverse rate (1.62 to 2.31). The ratio increased with depth gap, held inside single cells and held for sources with usable, uncut axons. Allen human slices had the same sign but an unresolved size (1.48, 0.86 to 2.52). In MICrONS, sources with unproofread axons gave a similar false bias (1.90, 1.75 to 2.06), but 520 sources with proofread axons gave none (0.94, 0.90 to 1.05). Limits: the Berlin tables probably include the original study's recordings; slices also truncate axons; we did not test a human EM volume.
